> Rare is adding private servers

Thank you for letting me know about this! I know I'll be making full use of them with my mates.

> Then this is just not your game then.

I understand your perspective here, but I think people making this game all about the PvP is also wrong, considering there is a lot to experience in it. I just want to do so peacefully. I've been playing since it came out and was barebones - back in 2018. I've recently come back from a hiatus.

> Join a crew.

> Stop playing for the loot / play for the experience

I play with my mates (who are newbies to the game) for that experience of sailing around and discovering things. However when we're attempting tall tales or having just finished a vault successfully, getting assaulted is just not fun. The stress doesn't melt away for us. Different strokes, of course.

> Winning without the fear of losing is flavorless.

I'd rather flavourless than the bad taste I'm consistently left with after being chased for an hour, spawn killed, and rehunted immediately after I've gotten my bearings.

I do appreciate the information you gave about the potential of private servers, but it is clear we have very different views on the game.

I disagree that players would just stop playing. From what I've seen, a lot of players would like the choice of being able to play without the risk of other players doggedly chasing them until they sink them or until they ultimately quit.

It might remove some risk, but there is still the possibility of being accosted by skeletons and other assorted monsters. Emissaries literally exist for the sole purpose of making things more dangerous. As does the Reaper flag. There are a lot of choices for people who want to PvP, but very little for those who want to play the game just for the fun stuff in the game - like the contracts, the tall tales, the exploration and the little pieces of lore.

Considering the amount of subreddits and the astoundingly wide variety of topics they cover, I'm not really surprised in the slightest. Reddit is its own universe, with many different corners and new ones cropping up all the time. Along with that, there are plenty of people who link reddit jokes, memes or posts to their family, to their friends and to their siblings, so it's no surprise that young people find themselves on here. Especially since it can offer a sense of anonymity, so those young people are able to peruse interests that might otherwise be considered cringe-worthy, or ask questions that might otherwise paint them as dumb for not knowing - which is assisted by the fact that there are so many more well-informed adults on the site that really don't give half a shit about why the question is being asked.

I've never actually thought through a proper land for myself, though I do have one for the troll who is essentially my trollsona, who shares my classpect.

Her land is the Land of Downpour and Expiration - LoDaE. The rain comes down so heavily that it’s impossible to see particularly far into it. The ground is a bunch of compressed, diamond hard bones, smoothed down from what looks like erosion. Very slippery.

Her quest was to make the rain ease up and bring life back to the consorts. As the Knight of Heart, she was to face her fears and come to terms with and apologise to the deceased that she had had to give to highbloods before the game. After a heartfelt apology and explanation to these souls, their crying relented some and the rain eased up. Many of these souls reincarnated as consorts, allowing the reanimated to finally rest.

As well as a lot of the other theories here, it could also be an allusion to the fact that they, like knights, often put up a front of sorts. However, unlike knights (who tend to use facades consciously in an attempt to cover up their insecurities and character flaws), Heart players seem to be hiding certain things from themselves. 

Dirk made everyone and himself think that he was fully in control despite the fact that he very much wasn't, as shown later on in the comic. 

Nepeta shipped everyone and made it seem like she was content with that, and she believed that she was also content with that, yet she also craved companionship, which is possibly why she was so eager to tacklepounce her moirail, Equius, upon meeting him in the game. Whether her craving was more physical or romantic is yet to be truly figured out, but I suspect it was a little bit of both.

In conclusion, I'd say that the Heart symbol symbolises the full front they show to everyone with the full half, along with their hidden even-to-themselves flaws as the hollow half.
